newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Cambodia asks ASEAN to mediate in conflict.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia asks ASEAN to mediate in conflict.

text.p: Cambodia, reversing a rebuff it issued last weekend, said on Wednesday it wants the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to mediate in the conflict between its two warring prime ministers.
"We have decided that we want to join ASEAN," said Foreign Minister Ung Huot, named to replace First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
"We have also decided that we want ASEAN to be a mediator."

Speaking to reporters after arriving in Kuala Lumpur for the annual ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting, Ung Huot said Phnom Penh's new stand on the issue reflected the wishes of Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
Hun Sen overthrew Ranariddh on July 6 after two days of heavy fighting in the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh.
"That is the new position," Ung Huot said, when asked if Hun Sen endorsed ASEAN's mediation efforts.
Last week, Hun Sen dismissed a mediation offer by an ASEAN delegation led by Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, saying foreigners should stay out of Cambodia's business.
"If we don't join (ASEAN), it won't be the death of us," he said.
Ung Huot said on Wednesday: "We want to join right now. That is the other firm desire of Hun Sen."
ASEAN postponed the admission of Cambodia, which was due to join on Wednesday along with Burma and Laos, after the July 5-6 fighting.
Asked if there was any chance of Cambodia joining ASEAN later on Wednesday, Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said: "No, no I don't think so."
"At 2:45 p.m. (0645 gmt) we are going to accept Myanmar (Burma) and Laos."
Alatas was speaking to reporters after meeting U.S. President Bill Clinton's special envoy on Cambodia, Stephen Solarz, who is shuttling around Asia seeking a solution to the crisis.
Thai Foreign Minister Prachaub Chaiyasan said on Wednesday the ASEAN foreign ministers would only discuss Cambodia's current status as an observer within the group.
"What we are going to discuss is about the observer status," Prachaub told reporters after addressing an ASEAN conference of diplomats, academics and businessmen.
An ASEAN diplomat said the foreign ministers would discuss at an informal lunch whether to accept Ung Huot as Cambodia's representative at the ASEAN meeting.
Hun Sen has backed Ung Huot to take Ranariddh's place as head of the royalist FUNCINPEC party and also take over the First Prime Minister's job.
Some 40 people, believed to be FUNCINPEC officials and supporters, have been summarily executed and a number of others have been tortured, aid workers and human rights groups in Cambodia said.
"I can tell you things are returning to normal in Cambodia now," Ung Huot said.
Solarz was holding talks with ASEAN foreign ministers on Wednesday in his effort to broker a solution.
"We very much want to work with our friends in ASEAN and other countries in region," the former U.S. congressman told reporters after meeting Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi.
ASEAN currently groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
